title: Superdry Hooded 5 Baffle Sports Puffer Army Khaki Green $99 (Was $249.95) Delivered @ Superdry
body:
Deal: Superdry Hooded 5 Baffle Sports Puffer Army Khaki Green $99 (Was $249.95) Delivered @ Superdry

[GunnerMcDagget] Superdry tends to be on the smaller side. Much smaller side. If you're a medium then in Superdry you're probably a Large or maybe XL.
If like me you're an XL, then Superdry doesn't make anything in your size.
[pongky] well if you look on that product page they do have 2XL, 3XL as well
[GunnerMcDagget] From my personal testing, 3XL is basically almost an XL. Still a bit too thin and way too short, but almost an XL
[BeefBiryani] Exactly. I have a medium macpac halo that fits me fine. but judging by the sizes here, I might need 2xl
[Drakesy] I'm a medium in everything, except superdry where i'm a large
[troyww] Seems completely at odds with this ;
Model Wears
Model height: 6ft 2in
Model wearing: M
Always pays to read peoples valuable comments .
Edit , I have a few SD polo's and @ 6'1 am a XL-2XL .
[excite] but in the product page, it says the Model of height: 6ft 2in (188cm) wearing M, so sounds like a size up is not needed
[GunnerMcDagget] Not so sure about the accuracy of that. Just look at any other size chart.
In Australia a medium has the average chest size of 114cm. SD lists it as 96-101cm
SD lists a medium waist size as 80-85cm. Australian standard medium waist size is 87cm.
That's before accounting for that fact that all SD clothing is shorter than the standard clothing in Australia. As a 6'3" person, every SD top or jacket I have tried is very short. Much shorter than the model picture suggests (keeping in mind that I haven't tried this specific jacket)
[cristobaljamesy] Seems like made for smaller peeps aka Asian sizing
[Xizor] Superdry sizing is all over the place. I have a few simple tshrts and they span 3 different sizes for basically the same fit.
[gadgetguy123] Superdrys biggest market is east and South Asia.
[fdawg] With five baffles, this puffer is unsinkable.
[motlking] I don't think keeping warm is a fad :)
Puffer jackets go on sale all the time. Style is subjective.
[FXx] What should I wear to keep warm instead? What's cheaper and more effective?
[Bogusjimmy] The puffer jacket is a 100 year old Aussie design. It's not going anywhere.
[INFIDEL] The incredible story of the Australian invention of the puffer jacket
Design is based on Himalayan mountaineering clothes from 100 years ago.
BUT "puffer jacket" is a genetic mid-70s US term for the destinctive warm street clothes.
New Zealand company Fairydown improved the original Himalayan exhibition design to create a jacket for Hillary's ascent of Everest in 1953. …that looks remarkably similar to today's puffer.
I have a Fairydown "down jacket" bought 20 years ago. Still wear it in cold.
Definitely was not sold as a "puffer jacket" but looks like one. Seems the term wasn't used here then.
MacPac base their Halo down jacket on a design by Fairydown.
[askvictor] I have one of those Fairydowns too; just from when Macpac had bought Fairydown and were retiring the brand. I thought they revived it at some point, but I seem to be mistaken.
[INFIDEL] @askvictor: MacPac acquired fellow NZ Fairydown almost 20 years ago, selling Fairydown gear through MacPac stores.
Fairydown brand was phased out.
Yes - name is occasionally used on some technical & other gear from MacPac. Trading on that long tradition in outdoor equipment. Probably works better in NZ where it was better know.
Wore my Fairydown down jacket into a Macpac store to compare with current Halo jacket. There was little difference in look, but mine had more loft despite so many winters in mountains.
Manager was excited to see it, but said to keep the better but much older Fairydown
[Morven] Lots of other jackets of various styles on sale at the same store.

[p3r514n] What's with the poly hate? It's more than adequate for suburban climates.
[skibidigrimacmoggr67] microplastics bad.
not joking either I am avoiding polyseter now in microfibre cloths and bedding.
you will probably agree if you ever seen how fine the fibres are that shedded they float lighter than dust does.
[skibidigrimacmoggr67] yeah I ignored it for awhile. then after 10th time of seeing it it finally got to me.
I could be breathing these fibres in directly, or it floats and sticks to dust wherever it is in your house, then keeps breaking down from there into even smaller microplastic fibres. then breath them in over time in the house.
keep in mind it's not happening day 1 of getting your jacket. but after years of use and exposed to sunlight and machine wash, they will start shedding eventually.
[p3r514n] @skibidigrimacmoggr67: Scary shit bro. Watching the Netflix doco didn't help.

[Kinjiru] I bought this exact jacket last year and wore it to Japan in Dec/Jan. It was great and was perfect for the very cold weather there. I've busted it out a few times in Sydney this winter on particularly cold days. Yes, Goose or Duck Down is better (lighter and it breathes), but if you want a puffer to stay warm, this has been pretty good to me.
[brandonstrandy] Polyester filling = literally useless. The whole point of a puffer jacket is real down feather filling which is excellent for warmth. Polyester does nothing. The fact that this was $250 to begin with is insanity.
I wouldn't even want this for free.
